title: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                11 AUG 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi
upsc_summary: Legislative Reform: The MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was passed by Parliament, updating the 2006 Act to boost MSME competitiveness and ease of doing business.
Revised Classification & Free Registration: Standardizes MSME criteria across investment and turnover; makes registration voluntary and completely free on the national Udyam portal.

Mandatory TReDS Settlement: Mandates Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) to settle MSME supplier invoices through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) platform to tackle delayed payments.

Dispute Resolution Framework: Permits States to set up multiple MSE Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs) and introduces strict statutory timelines: 90 days for mediation, referral to arbitration within 30 days upon failure, and 90 days for arbitral awards.

Legal Protection & Recovery: Requires courts to direct payment of at least 50% of the awarded amount to MSMEs during pending set-aside applications (>6 months); permits recovery of mediated settlements/awards as 'arrears of land revenue'.
Decriminalisation: Replaces criminal penal provisions for non-filing or minor non-disclosures with warnings and administrative fines.

The Alang-Sosiya cluster in Gujarat accounts for ~98% of India's ship recycling capacity, producing around 3.5 MMT of steel per annum without raw material exploitation.

Ship-breaking Credit Note Scheme (under SBFA 2.0): Grants credit notes worth 40% of recycled scrap value to incentivize domestic shipbuilding and compliant recycling.
